title: Family Cookbook · First design direction
question: Compare the same mobile review task. Choose a world to carry through Cookbook, Add photo, Review and Recipe on mobile and desktop. These are synthetic design proposals, not working product screens.

options.label: Woven work surface
options.lineage: Woven table settings and contrasting edge bands
options.thesis: A stable shared work surface gives original and draft their own places.
options.viewport: A portrait review screen with a deep petrol title band, Source / Draft switch and aligned ingredient rows.
options.risk: The textile cue must stay at the margins so the screen never feels ornamental.

raised.raise: Keep one dominant task and remove competing primary actions.
Separate destructive controls and keep source and draft roles stable.
Use a consistent spatial group for each task without decorating every field.
Keep processing state visible across navigation and never remove an unfinished draft silently.
Keep the original immutable and make review changes a visibly separate layer.
Pair uncertainty color with explicit text and iconography.

options.label: Archive register
options.lineage: Library accession records and family document archives
options.thesis: The original and its reviewed transcription read as two linked records.
options.viewport: A portrait review register with source index, named sections and legible quantities aligned against their units.
options.risk: Familiar document organization is effective but may feel administrative unless family attribution remains visible.

options.label: Vertical recipe viewer
options.thesis: One recipe source fills each viewport, with review actions on a side rail.
options.viewport: Full-bleed source with a low caption and four rail controls.
options.risk: Snap navigation hides adjacent ingredients and makes comparison harder.
options.case: Family identification and review clarity both trail the shared work-surface direction.
options.kept: Keep one dominant task and remove competing primary actions.

options.label: Graphite comparison desk
options.thesis: Persistent source and draft panels form a compact verification desk.
options.viewport: Graphite panels with small headers and a single approval accent.
options.risk: Dense technical panel language adds reading effort for occasional family users.
options.case: A technical console is less familiar to this audience; compact panel density weakens mobile review clarity.
options.kept: Separate destructive controls and keep source and draft roles stable.

options.label: Recipe garden map
options.thesis: A large flat-color region groups each recipe and its review actions.
options.viewport: A dominant green lobe contains the current recipe, with capsule actions.
options.risk: Organic boundaries consume space needed for long ingredients and fields.
options.case: A visitor-map metaphor is less relevant to family preservation and less clear for textual correction.
options.kept: Use a consistent spatial group for each task without decorating every field.

options.label: Import departure board
options.thesis: A fixed status board tracks drafts and keeps changed jobs visible.
options.viewport: Segmented recipe header with fixed columns and a persistent changed-state label.
options.risk: Travel ranking implies urgency and throughput that family review does not require.
options.case: Departure ranking is less recognizable as family preservation and obscures source comparison.
options.kept: Keep processing state visible across navigation and never remove an unfinished draft silently.

options.label: Source and review course
options.thesis: An immutable source sits below a numbered course through review sections.
options.viewport: Numbered review controls and a fixed source with a separate active layer.
options.risk: Map-like navigation and encoded symbols add interpretation work.
options.case: The outdoor course is a weaker family context and numbered symbols are less direct than named review sections.
options.kept: Keep the original immutable and make review changes a visibly separate layer.

options.label: Exposure review sheets
options.thesis: Overlapping source and draft sheets use non-color marks for unresolved areas.
options.viewport: Neutral sheets overlap above a zone scale; hatching marks conflicts.
options.risk: Overlaps hide text and fractional exposure notation competes with recipe quantities.
options.case: Darkroom notation is unfamiliar to most families and overlapping sheets weaken field legibility.
options.kept: Pair uncertainty color with explicit text and iconography.

canonCard.label: Familiar recipe app
canonCard.thesis: A conventional light recipe interface with straightforward forms and standard navigation.
canonCard.viewport: A standard review title, Source / Draft control, stacked fields and bottom Save recipe action.
canonCard.risk: Familiar and easy to recognize, with little distinctive visual identity.
